newsitem.title: INDIA: ITC-Threadneedle comments on India oil price hike.
newsitem.headline: ITC-Threadneedle comments on India oil price hike.

text.p: Uncertainty over a long overdue hike in oil prices planned by the Indian government has capped fresh stockmarket demand, Ajay Srinivasan, chief investment officer of ITC-Threadneedle Asset Management said on Wednesday.
"Yes, the oil price hike has been discounted, but the minute it comes, the market is bound to adjust," Srinivasan said.
Prime Minister Inder Kumar Gujral said on Tuesday his United Front coalition's policy-setting steering committee would take a decision on hiking petroleum product prices on June 15.

"The issue of increase in prices of petroleum products will be decided finally at the steering committee meeting on June 15," the Press Trust of India quoted Gujral as telling reporters after the induction of four ministers into his cabinet.
Strong opposition from left-wing constituents of the United Front had prevented the steering committee from achieving a consensus on raising the prices of oil products at its last meeting on May 25.
"Today, no one really knows anything about the quantum, the method and how exactly the hike will affect companies," Srinivasan said.

Gujral on Tuesday vowed to stick to his stand of evolving a consensus among various political parties on the issue of increasing petroleum product prices to tackle the soaring oil subsidy bill, which has brought about divisions in the centre-left multi-party coalition.
"I think if it's done and done quickly, it shows the government's resolve to tackle important problems," Srinivasan said.
"By delaying it, they are only sending a message that they are not facing the issue upfront."

Analysts said the government must decide soon how to pay money owed to oil companies -- a total of 155 billion rupees ($4.33 billion) at the end of March -- for selling subsided petroleum products well below global prices.
The deficit is expected to rise to 245 billion rupees by March 31, 1998.
